A directory with an `index.js`, like a package, decides what it shows to the outside. An import that reaches past it, such as `./api/users` or `lodash/get`, depends on how the inside is laid out and breaks when a file in there is moved or renamed.

An import path may have one step: `./api`, `../api`, `lodash`, `@scope/package`. A longer path is reported if the file exists. `export ... from`, `import()` and `require()` are checked too.

## Examples

Reported:

{/* file "api/index.js" */}
```js api/index.js
export { listUsers } from "./users";
```

{/* file "api/users.js" */}
```js api/users.js
export const listUsers = () => fetch("/users");
```

{/* bad */}
```js
import { listUsers } from "./api/users";
```

Not reported:

{/* file "api/index.js" */}
```js api/index.js
export { listUsers } from "./users";
```

{/* file "api/users.js" */}
```js api/users.js
export const listUsers = () => fetch("/users");
```

{/* good */}
```js
import { listUsers } from "./api";
```

## Options

| Option | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `allow` | `[]` | Globs. A longer path is allowed if one matches the import path, without its `./` or `../`, or the full path of the file. |
| `forbid` | none | Globs, matched the same way. Only what matches one is reported, and every other path is allowed. |

Use `allow` or `forbid`, not both.

With `{ "allow": ["api/*"] }`:

{/* file "api/users.js" */}
```js api/users.js
export const listUsers = () => fetch("/users");
```

{/* good {"options": [{"allow": ["api/*"]}]} */}
```js
import { listUsers } from "./api/users";
```

With `{ "forbid": ["db/*"] }`, only the second import is reported:

{/* file "api/users.js" */}
```js api/users.js
export const listUsers = () => fetch("/users");
```

{/* file "db/pool.js" */}
```js db/pool.js
export const pool = [];
```

{/* bad {"count": 1, "options": [{"forbid": ["db/*"]}]} */}
```js
import { listUsers } from "./api/users";
import { pool } from "./db/pool";
```
